cost a lot verb

also cost little, cost more, cost less, it costs a lot, be dear, at that price, cheaply, at a high price, at a low price, more cheaply, cost nothing, cost (verb)

magnō (parvō) cōnstāre

phrase: cōnstō with the ablative of price · Wiktionary

cost a lot (little)

With verbs of buying, selling and costing, the price is in the ablative: magnō, parvō, plūrimō, minimō, vīlī. Only tantī, quantī, plūris, minōris are genitive (see below and how much is it?).

Other words

  • plūris (minōris) cōnstāre — cost more (less)

    phrase: cōnstō with the genitive of price; so also tantī, quantī · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 13.29.2: prope dīmidiō minōris cōnstābit (Lewis & Short); Traupman 297 · Wiktionary

    Quantī cōnstat?, how much does it cost?; tantī, at that price.

  • magnī (parvī) cōnstāre — cost a lot (little)

    avoid · modern · Traupman 130 (to cost a lot, little …: the genitive); Traupman 297 · Wiktionary

    The genitives magnī, parvī are for valuing (magnī aestimāre, see value); for costing, Lewis & Short gives the ablative, and the genitive only for tantī, quantī, plūris, minōris.

Examples

  • Haec māla parvō cōnstant.

    These apples are cheap.composed

  • parvō famēs cōnstat, magnō fastīdium

    hunger costs little, fussiness a lotSen. Ep. 17.4

  • ego … paenitēre tantī nōn emō

    I don’t buy regret at that priceGell. 1.8.6

  • vīvitur parvō bene

    one lives well on littleHor. C. 2.16.13

  • minōris pretiī

    more cheaplyTraupman 289

See also expensive, cheap, how much is it?, price, value.
